criteria.notes: 2 tests: delivers agent event with sessionId/taskId/event, delivers system init events. Verified via real ws client receiving JSON messages from processManager 'event' emit.
1 test: delivers error messages with sessionId and taskId. Asserts event is undefined (shared agentHandler destructures {sessionId, event} but error payloads carry {sessionId, error}).
2 tests: delivers terminal data with type/sessionId/data, preserves ANSI escape sequences intact through WebSocket JSON serialization.
2 tests: forwards terminal-input messages to writeToTerminal with correct sessionId/data, handles multiple sequential inputs.
2 tests: forwards terminal-resize messages to resizeTerminal with correct cols/rows, handles different dimension values.

criteria.criterion: AC6 — Multiple Clients Receive Agent Events
criteria.notes: 3 tests: 2-client broadcast, 3-client broadcast, verifies disconnected client does NOT receive new events (negative assertion with baseline snapshot).

3 tests: verifies exactly 3 off calls (event/error/terminal-data), verifies handler references match (captured before splice), verifies per-client handler isolation (shared vs unshared). Resets offCalls before close to isolate from afterEach cleanup.

criteria.criterion: AC8 — Malformed Message Does Not Crash
criteria.notes: 2 tests: malformed JSON ({type: "terminal-input") does not crash, empty object string ({}) does not crash. Both verify server remains functional via subsequent valid message.

criteria.criterion: AC9 — Non-JSON Data Does Not Crash
criteria.notes: 2 tests: raw text 'hello-not-json' does not crash, binary data (\x00-\x04) does not crash. Both verify server remains functional via subsequent valid message.

criteria.criterion: AC10 — Session ID to Task ID Resolution
criteria.notes: 1 test: getSession returns {taskId} → client message includes resolved taskId.
1 test: getSession returns undefined → taskId is undefined in client message (graceful handling).

summary: All 11 acceptance criteria PASS. 21 tests across 11 describe blocks. Zero TypeScript errors. Uses real HTTP server + WSS with ws clients (no transport mocks). The mock processManager injects controlled events to verify the server→client streaming paths end-to-end.
